**Goal.** Make the port work across the process boundary — preload surface, single-flight `agent:prompt` handler, `selectAdapter`, IPC client.

## Decisions this slice realizes

Quoted from the master by their own headings; the master's prose under each
one governs, and the Contracts that name them are there too.

### D4 The chat pane always speaks over IPC; its port is handed to it · proposed

### D5 Two launch flavors, fake by default, remote debugging always on · aligned

### D6 One turn at a time, correlated by turn id · proposed

### D7 Preload exposes exactly one object · proposed

**Done looks like** — these are this run's done-criteria, and nothing else is:
- an agent runs `npm run dev`, `agent-browser connect 9222`, `snapshot -i`, fills the input with "Hello agent", clicks send and `wait --text` sees the canned reply stream into the pane — no paid call anywhere
- `mountApp` builds the IPC client and hands it to the pane; the pane still imports only the port
- preload exposes exactly one `window.crucible.agent` object with `prompt` and `onEvent`, forwarding payloads only
- a unit test on the handler with the fake adapter shows a prompt arriving mid-turn answered with turn_started then error code "busy" while the live turn runs on
- reloading the window mid-turn disposes the turn, releases the guard, and the remounted pane starts empty and can prompt immediately
